description: Join Riverside Park Conservancy and the Climate Film Festival for a special preview screening of four short films exploring our local environment and the people working to help cities and wildlife adapt to a changing climate. A conversation with filmmakers will follow, including:Emily Driscoll, director, Snow BearsEmily Fano, RiSC, producer, Where It FloodsEliza Mitnick, director, A Fragile ParadiseJason Jaacks, director, Between Moon TidesMaggie Burnette Stogner, director, Refuge KeepersMore to be announced!Snow Bears (2026)Artist Heide Hatry, known as “Snow Banksy,” crafts polar bears out of snow to draw attention to a warming world. What begins as a solitary pandemic project grows into community climate action, as she inspires more than 100 New Yorkers to build snow bears alongside her in Central Park. She dreams of seeing snow bears spread around the globe.Where It Floods: Planting Hope in Coney Island (2023)Where it Floods follows New York City students on the frontline of climate activism in Coney Island as they participate in RiSC, the National Wildlife Federation's award-winning climate education program that connects schools with local residents and partner organizations to help build community resilience.A Fragile Paradise (2026)Beyond its summer crowds and postcard-perfect beaches, Fire Island is sustained by the people who quietly care for it year-round. A Fragile Paradise follows landscaper Dylan Wallace, who helps preserve the island's fragile dunes; Margaret Hofbeck, whose monarch butterfly garden has become a sanctuary for endangered butterflies; and longtime shopkeepers Lynn and Wes Little, whose dockside market has served as the heart of Seaview for generations. Together, their stories reveal the many ways people care for a place, from protecting delicate ecosystems to preserving the traditions and relationships that define a place. Through intimate observational moments and sweeping coastal imagery, A Fragile Paradise is a portrait of Fire Island through the people who sustain it—a reflection on stewardship, resilience, and our relationship to the places we call home.Between Moon Tides (2025)Between Moon Tides follows an intergenerational group of citizen scientists in coastal New England as they attempt to save the Saltmarsh Sparrow from extinction — one nest at a time. Against the backdrop of rising sea levels, three retirees and a young intern forge deep bonds while scouring the saltmarsh, banding birds, and witnessing firsthand the devastating effects of climate change. Through stunning visuals and intimate storytelling, the film reveals how a disappearing bird serves as both a warning and a call to action. Yet, at its heart, Between Moon Tides is a love story—about nature, mentorship, and the hope that comes from refusing to give up, even in the face of impossible odds.Refuge Keepers (2026)Where the sea is both livelihood and legacy, veteran fishermen, women community leaders, and young conservationists unite in Celestún, Mexico to create a pioneering marine refuge, hoping to save the waters that sustain their community and way of life.

description: Bryant Park's first-ever Brass Festival brings three incredible incredible brass ensembles to the main stage. From Brass Queens' female-led upbeat horns, to Aberdeen's inventive jazz/indie rock blend, and finishing with the New Orleans-born, Grammy-nominated New Breed Brass Band, this high-energy celebration of modern brass is the perfect way to herald in the end of summer. New Breed Brass Band fuses NOLA’s fertile brass band tradition with Caribbean, hip-hop, and modern R&B in the vein of Bruno Mars and Anderson .Paak. The explosive group makes music by and for the Crescent City’s next generation: joyful, vital and unstoppable. New Breed Brass Band is led by drummer Jenard Andrews, son of Tremé trumpet legend James Andrews and nephew of New Orleans scene lynchpin Trombone Shorty. Under Trombone Shorty’s tutelage a new sound was born, and audiences took notice.The band has toured North America and Europe and opened for The Fray, Blackalicious and Dr. John. With the band’s debut album, 2023’s Made In New Orleans, New Breed is hewing a new path for 21st century second-lines, and everyone’s invited to join the procession.Aberdeen is a Brooklyn-based horn band known for its soulful melody-driven instrumental arrangements. Aberdeen's music is about community; a large collective of musicians featuring Allison Philips on trumpet, Olivia Hughart, Jared Yee, Mackenzie McCarthy, Brian Plautz & Stephen Chen on saxes, Jacob Melsha & Jasmi Perales on trombones, Shubh Saran on guitar, Ronnie Lanzilotta on bass and Ross Pederson on drums. Aberdeen's albums Downpour and Held Together showcase their energetic, massive, one-of-a-kind sound.Hailing from Brooklyn, NY, the award-winning Brass Queens are a female-led brass band featuring all-female horns with a sound that sits right at the intersection of the Big Apple and the Big Easy. Their music is deeply inspired by and pays homage to the New Orleans brass band tradition while injecting the upbeat, multifaceted energy of their New York home into each performance. Brass Queens tour regularly across the country and internationally, increasing the visibility of female musicians in the industry.Bryant Park Picnic Performances presented by Bank of America is a free outdoor festival that welcomes all New Yorkers to experience the city’s vibrant arts and culture. The series provides a platform for extraordinary artists and serves as a vital outdoor venue for a wide array of New York’s cultural institutions.

GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.Register here!This is a great opportunity to support a dynamic community space while learning about urban agriculture. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Location: 780 Blake Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11207For information about group volunteering, please contact Volunteer Program Coordinator, Olivia Navarro at Olivia.Navarro@parks.nyc.govThis event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

description: Join West Harlem Arts Alliance, Harlem Late Night Jazz and NYC Parks for the annual jazz festival.    The Jazz Festival takes place in Morningside, St. Nicholas, Jackie Robinson from May to September. In Montefiore Square Park, the jazz festival is from June - August, weekly on Saturdays at 6 pm. In the Historic Harlem Parks of Morningside, St. Nicholas and Jackie Robinson, there are monthly jazz events. Morningside Park is typically second Saturdays from 5-6:30 pm at 113 Street and Morningside Ave, within the park. St. Nicholas is typically on fourth Fridays from 6-7:30 pm at the James Baldwin Lawn and 135 Street Plaza located at 135 Street and St. Nicholas Ave. Jackie Robinson Park is typically on first Fridays from 6-7:30 pm at the Bandshell, located at 148 Street and Bradhurst Ave. ADA access is located at 150 Street and Bradhurst Ave. Visit whaanyc.org for the full schedule of events and artist line up. September 12 at Morningside Park features Carlos Jimenez Mambo.
